summary: Tested WiiM Now Playing (backend demo status/play-pause/auth + Listen UI at 390px & 1920px), Camera Snapshot Share (desktop download, mocked Capacitor Share/Filesystem, recordings AppLauncher regression), regressions (iter23 listen suite 15/15, room tabs, Party, Shortcuts, Thermostat, Settings, Settings WiiM Check), and static review of the windows/ auto-start scripts. Everything requested works. 2 minor issues found.

minor.issue: After linkplay.command succeeds, it returns await wiim_status(wid). If the status read then fails (424), the user gets an error toast even though the toggle was already sent. Could only be checked in the code; LIVE mode can't run here.

Demo vs live is decided by the amp's live flag (live(doc) = _amp.live), not by the WiiM itself. If the amp is LIVE but the WiiMs are not set up, now-playing silently disappears because of a 404. This is acceptable but worth knowing.

ui_bugs.issue: If the video isn't ready (readyState<2), it falls back to video.poster. The poster is a hard-coded Unsplash STOCK photo (CameraPlayer STILL), so in LIVE mode, if the feed is still loading or has failed, the user shares a stock photo stamped 'Front Entry · <date time>' as if it were a real camera snapshot. Suggest: in LIVE mode throw 'The live feed isn't playing yet', or use a real Protect snapshot endpoint instead of the poster.

issues: The play/pause circle (top-right, 40px) nearly touches the 'Mobile Device' label: they overlap by about 4px horizontally and 7px vertically in bounding boxes. A longer source label would run under the button. Consider pr-12 on the label when streaming.

action_items: Don't share the stock poster image as a camera snapshot in LIVE mode (snapshot.js poster fallback)
Optional: add right padding to the source label when the play/pause button is shown
Optional: in LIVE play-pause, don't error if only the follow-up status read fails
critical_code_review_comments: Snapshot poster fallback = stock image (see ui_bugs).
The Capacitor path writes a new camera-*.jpg to CACHE on every snapshot and never removes old ones. This is minor because the OS clears the cache.

crossOrigin=anonymous on <video> is fine: the hls.js/MSE path is untainted, and /api/camera/hls* sends ACAO for LAN origins (checked with Origin http://192.168.0.10:3000). Native Safari HLS depends on this CORS header, which is present.

windows/*.ps1/.cmd: ASCII only (safe for PS 5.1). Tasks are AtStartup, SYSTEM, highest privileges, 20s delay, restart 999, no time limit. PATH and serve are saved to path.cmd. The loop/restart and log rotation look correct. These scripts were reviewed only and not run. Caveat: path.cmd stores the admin's PATH at install time, so re-run the installer after installing new tools.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows; 1 medium logic issue (stock poster fallback)

seed_data_creation: None. Ran listen restore-defaults at the end. wiim1/wiim2 are left playing=true. Still in DEMO mode.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Source testids: office Mobile Device=source-office-5-1, office TV=source-office-5-0, bathroom Mobile=source-bathroom-6, living Mobile=source-living-3, master Mobile=source-master-4. Headless Chromium can't decode the mux H264 demo HLS (video readyState stays 0), so the snapshot used the poster fallback. The real video-frame capture path was NOT exercised in the browser. Capacitor mock via add_init_script works (window.__capSnap caches plugins). Run test_iter24 with -n0 or alongside other suites; its log assertion tolerates concurrent writes.
